en: Eve: Now, let's settle this once\nand for all.

I'm not the same person I was
last year, Eve! Can you still say
the same thing after seeing me
like this?!
Eve: Ugh...! No matter what you\nlook like, I won't lose!!
Heh heh heh... I look forward to\nseeing how long that bravado\nlasts.
Now, let the battle begin...!
*Sigh*... What kind of\nentertainment is this?

Apparently, it's a Hagoita duel
between Eve and Coro. They
couldn't settle it last year, so
they're doing it for real this
time...
Hagoita, huh... Though, Coro\nseems to be wearing something\nrather extreme for that.

Um, it seems to be called the
Hagoita Summit Decisive Battle
Weapon, "<font color=yellow>Shofuku Zetto
Darmizer '56</font>".

According to this manual, they
built a special alloy body,
layered it with Crest Arts
barriers, and then connected
Coro's AI to it...

I don't really follow, but I can
tell that's definitely not
equipment meant for playing
Hagoita,
And that Eve's physical abilities\nare just as insane for keeping\nup with it.
So, Captain. You're the referee\nfor this century's duel, then?
There's no need to use such\nviolent words as "duel."

Getting a bit of moderate
exercise during a New Year's
spent eating and sleeping... it's
a good thing, isn't it?
I'll settle it here!\nHaaaaaaaaaaaaah!!
This is nothing!\nHyaaaaaaaaaaaaah!!
I think you're also quite\nsomething, calling this disaster\n"moderate exercise."

Still, it's a lovely place. I didn't
expect such an open area to
exist at the top of a mountain
range.

It's a good place for a
vacation. I don't dislike the Sea
of Stars, but I prefer to spend
my leisure time with my feet on
the ground.

Just in case, I've hidden the
ship with transparent rigging,
but the steep mountains
should keep it hidden from
everything but the sky.

Besides, this planet's
civilization is like Earth's Middle
Ages, so there's no chance of
being discovered...
Hmph, I wonder about that.
Eh?
O-Oh, heavens...
Hm, are these the local\ninhabitants!?
No way, they climbed up these\nsteep mountains!?
Local Old Man: Over here! They\nwere over here! No... they were\nright hereeeee!!

Local Woman: Ah, how divine...
You are the group of
goddesses the <font color=yellow>Shrine Maiden</font>
spoke of!
Wait, what is going on!?
This is bad. Coro, hide yourself!\nContact the others who are\nresting elsewhere!
Y-Yessir!!!

Local Old Man: Oh! As
expected of a warrior serving
the goddesses! One shout, and
you've exorcised that evil
being!
Eh? No...

Local Man: Gramps, let's talk
later! Come on, everyone, don't
just stand there! The Shrine
Maiden told us!

Local Man: The beautiful
goddesses of war are weary
from fighting evil. Hurry, let's
invite them to our feast to help
them recover!
Local Residents: Yeah!!

Local Woman: Come now,
Goddess. We have prepared a
palanquin for you. Please, step
inside!
Hey, what is actually going on\nhere!?
What should we do, Captain! At\nthis rate, they're really going to\ntake us away!
You want us to just follow\nthem...? Is that really okay!?

Look at their desperate faces.
There must be a reason. As
the Captain says, let's at least
hear them out.
Eleyna, can you see\nsomething?

Who knows? Come on, let's go.
Celebrating the New Year with
the local sake doesn't sound
half bad.
The priestess spoke: "On the\nday of the new moon, in the\nmonth of harmony."

Upon the mountain peak where
the sun rises, three
constellations descend
alongside the solar disk.
These three celestial maidens\nwere sent to battle the wicked\ndemons that plague this land.
With the power gained from\nthe people's divine offerings\nand healing feasts,
The princesses shall strike\ndown the demons and restore\npure winds to this land.
First crop failures, now a\nplague... It seems this country\nis in quite a state of chaos.

And we just happened to be at
the exact spot the
"Kannagi"―or whatever that
famous fortune teller is
called―prophesied...
The people here seem to\nbelieve they can escape this\ncrisis just by hosting us...

Situational assessment
complete! It seems the
large-scale crop failures in this
region are due to climate
change.

The plague stems from
malnutrition due to food
shortages; no traces of
advanced civilizations were
found.

So you are saying the people
of this country are facing
hardships that lie at the end of
a correct evolution?
That is precisely what it\ncomes down to...

Captain, it's a hard choice, but
saving them violates the
Unadvanced Planet Protection
Treaty.

Eve: "Captain, if we wait for the
right moment to slip away...
that means abandoning the
people of this country!!"
Hey, Eve, keep your voice\ndown. They'll hear you.
Eve: "But..."

...That is the providence of
nature. If we intervene and
force unnatural evolution, it
could lead to even more
catastrophic consequences.

All we can do is leave quietly
and pray that they overcome
these hardships through their
own strength.

By recklessly helping people in
an undeveloped civilization, we
might distort their path of
evolution...
It's true that Baschen might\nhave been in that very state\nsince Givel appeared...

They left everything to Givel
and stopped thinking for
themselves, only to be used as
they pleased.

Local Elder: "What is the
matter, Goddess?! If you keep
such a gloomy expression, your
luck will surely fade!"

Local Woman: "This meal is
quite humble and may not suit
your palate, but please, do
have some."

The Elder and his
granddaughter, right? It seems
there are no plates for you
two; won't you eat?

Elder's Granddaughter: To
share a meal with a Goddess...
it is far too great an honor...
Please, do not mind us...
Is something troubling you?
Elder: Ah, no... It is a trivial\nmatter, but...

Elder: We heard three
Goddesses would descend, so
we wonder why things differ
from the Priestess's prophecy...

Elder's Granddaughter: It is
true; the Priestess's prophecy
has never once been wrong
before.
...Three Goddesses, huh?
What's with that look, Crowe?\nI'm a perfectly fine Goddess\nmyself.

Nobleman: The old man is just
a worrier! Don't mind him, O
Gods! Now, let us present one
of this country's finest
dancers!

*Sigh*... The country is in crisis,
yet they're making a fuss over
fortune-telling... I wonder if this
is what faith is all about.
Reimi, are you taking a break\nhere too?
Ah, Karlyn.

...I was just wondering if it's
really okay for the people of
this country to be doing this
when things are so dire.
Even if they pray to us, it won't\nprovide any real help...
So you're thinking the same\nthing I am.
Warrior-like Man: Goddess,\nmight I have a moment of your\ntime?
Eh, who are you?
Warrior-like Man: I am <font color=yellow>Yamato</font>,\nservant to the Miko. She\nwishes to meet you, Goddess...
The Miko... The one who\nprophesied our arrival.
You're finally here.
Yamato: Wh-who are you?
It'll make the discussion with\nthis Miko go more smoothly if\nI'm there. I'll come along.
Eleyna, what do you mean? If\nyou know something...
I'm sure the Miko will explain\nthe circumstances. Come on,\nlet's go.
Yamato: Understood. Please,\nfollow me this way.
Yamato: This is it. Please\nwatch your step, as it is dark\nunderfoot.
What is this? I can't believe a\nplace like this exists at the end\nof a cave...!
I wonder if the writing on the\nwalls is the script of this\ncountry?

Please, do not touch them.
Your immense power might
weaken the power of the
"Oracle."

It is an honor to meet you. I am
the one who serves as the
shrine maiden of this land, and
my name is <font color=yellow>Iyo</font>.

Iyo: I sincerely apologize for
involving travelers from the
Sea of Stars in the affairs of
our nation.
Eh, the Sea of Stars!? How\nmuch do you actually know\nabout us!?

Iyo: I understand that you are
outsiders who possess an ark
to cross the Sea of Stars and
have come to this land to rest.
How could you possibly know\nthat...?

This person spoke of an
"Oracle" just now, didn't they?
They possess the same power
as I do―the ability to see
through all past and future.

Iyo: Unfortunately, I am merely
a descendant. I do not possess
the power to hear the Oracles
myself.

Iyo: All I can do is decipher the
records of the future left upon
these walls by the first shrine
maiden.

So you're saying... you've
known about us... no, about this
entire universe, for a very long
time?
Ichiyo: Yes, that is correct.

Ichiyo: If the people learned
this, chaos would ensue. Thus,
only the Priestess and her
guardians may enter this
shrine.
You've made yourself clear.\nWhy don't we get to the main\npoint?
Ichiyo: Thank you.

Ichiyo: I intend to suppress the
worship of the Priestess in this
country and incite a rebellion
among the people.
What?! The country is already\nin chaos! And now you're\ntalking about a rebellion too?!

Ichiyo: Precisely. With the
nation in turmoil and
discontent mounting, now is
the perfect time to start a
rebellion.
...What do you mean? Ichiyo,\nwhat on earth are you trying to\ndo?

Ichiyo: Priestess records say
this nation falls in 278 days. In
the ensuing chaos, 90% of the
population is recorded to
perish.

90% of the people?! If things
end up like that, it's only a
matter of time before the
survivors die out too...
Ichiyo: Yes. That is why I wish\nto overturn this oracle.

An oracle is but one possibility
for the future. However,
overturning it requires power
far beyond the ordinary.
Iyo: Yes, which is why I intend\nto incite the rejection of faith\nand a popular uprising.

I thought three people had just
vanished during yesterday's
banquet, but this was actually
happening.
Still, that Priestess is one\ngutsy individual.

During crop failures, she holds
a massive banquet under the
priestess's direction to draw all
the people's resentment
toward herself.

Then, she shows them us being
defeated by the Akki, slamming
home the fact that the
prophecy was wrong... I see.

With the people so blindly
devoted to the Priestess, the
shock when the prophecy fails
will be immense.

Furthermore, it seems the core
members of the rebel army
have already been arranged
under Yamato's orders.
The plan is to use Yamato's\nelite force to defeat the Akki,\nturning them into heroes.

Thorough to the end. She's
calculating that having a hero
ready to lead will minimize the
chaos following the rebellion.

That shrine likely foretold a
future where people cling to
oracles, doing nothing but
praying to the gods.

If a great transformation
occurs in the consciousness of
the people, it may be possible
to overturn the oracle.

But what will happen to Iyo?
They're going to make
everyone resent her as a
shrine maiden to incite a
rebellion, right? I don't think it'll
end without consequences.

It looks like they'll make it
seem like Yamato defeated
her, while actually arranging to
transfer her to another
country when the rebellion
breaks out.

This is a local issue, and
getting involved recklessly
could violate the Uncharted
Planet Protection Treaty.
But, I want to help Iyo-san.

Because I believe this fight will
help this country break free
from the oracles' superhuman
power and return to the path
of true evolution.
So, Captain, please... everyone...

The Captain is right. We'll help
even if you don't ask. We can't
just abandon the lives right in
front of us.

So, what about that "evil
demon" who's always so loud
about Uncharted Planet
Protection?
Of course, if the Captain says\nit's okay, we're in this together!\nNo problem at all!

We can use
'Darmizer'56'―whom the
country believes is the
incarnation of evil―to make it
look like

Making it look like we beat
Leesh and the others, or even
acting like Yamato's group
defeated us, will be a piece of
cake!
Though, being defeated by\nCoro is something I'd rather\navoid.
I heard Ichiyo's words of\nresolve with my own ears. I\nhave no reason to oppose this.

It's been since you stopped
Asmodeus's resurrection that
we've seen an oracle
overturned. I look forward to it.
Reimi, we are all of one heart.\nWe fight to seize the true\nfuture of this country!
Thank you, everyone!
Now, let us settle this. In the\nname of God, I cannot overlook\nany further folly!
Come, let us fight fairly...!

(Hey, what's wrong, Coro?! Did
you forget your lines?!
Everyone is watching, so get it
together!!)
(Ugh, hey!! This isn't what we\nrehearsed!)
(Karlyn! Everyone is watching!\nFor now, let's just fight!!)
Argh!!
Are you okay, Karlyn!? Coro,\nstop it! You're going way too\nfar!!
Everyone!! It's an\ne-e-emergency!! Please run\naway right now!!
The transmission finally\nconnected! Hey, you, have you\nno sense of moderation...!!
That's not it, Eve! It's not me!\nIt's moving without being linked\nto my AI!!
Wait, that outer shell is moving\non its own!?

It seems so. I'm investigating
the cause, but a special barrier
is preventing access to the
control mechanism...
Can you see something,\nEleyna!?
No, I don't know...
(But, for even I to be unable to\nread it...)
You're right, Captain! Let's\nprioritize evacuating the people\nof the country first!

We'll secure the retreat path.
Yamato, take your unit and
make sure everyone gathered
here escapes safely!
Yamato: I cannot retreat.

Don't be so stubborn! We don't
even know the situation
ourselves! First, you all need to
get to a safe place...

Yamato: If we hide behind your
protection, our nation will never
break free from its faith in the
gods and the miko!
But with your current\nequipment, standing against\nthat weapon is...
Yamato: However, this is a\nbattle for our very future!
Yamato: Everyone, follow\nmeeeee!!
Ugh...! We can't leave it all to\nthem! Captain, let's fight!
Elite Warrior: Seiyaaaaaa!

The enemy flinched! As
expected of the elite unit.
Their training and morale are
even higher than I imagined.

But with such a small number,
they can only hold out for so
long! Captain, I'll go command
the evacuation in the rear.
Elite Warrior: Guah...! Is this...\nthe end...?

Yamato: Stand up! Do not
falter!! Raise your heads and
stare down the enemy! Our
future lies only there!
...!! Damn it... we can't lose...!\nWaaaaaaah!!
Everyone, let's hurry down the\nmountain! I will guide you, so\nplease follow my instructions!

...Why are they fighting? The
Priestess's prophecy said the
Goddess would destroy the
demons.
If we just follow the Priestess,\nall will be well... What are those\npeople doing...?!

Elder, do you truly believe this
situation will be resolved
without anyone doing
anything?
...G-Goddess. I... I...

Regardless, it's dangerous
here! Prioritize the injured and
the young children, and
evacuate!
Goddess! I will go and gather\neveryone who can use healing\narts!
Please do!
You, what are you doing?!

I'm going to lend Yamato a
hand! With this bad harvest, I
was worried my body was
getting stiff from not swinging
a hoe enough!

That's a help, but know when
to retreat! Please, don't let
your bravery turn into mere
recklessness!

Elder: What are you thinking?!
Do you doubt the Goddess's
victory?! Do you dare doubt
the Priestess's prophecy?!

Elder, this isn't about belief. If
our comrades are fighting right
before our eyes, it's only
natural to lend a hand.
Well then, I will go and guide\neveryone to safety.

Young Man: I'm coming too!
Gramps, you make sure to help
the Goddess! Everyone will
listen to you if you tell them to!
Eh, reinforcements?! Yamato,\nwere you still preparing\ntroops?

Yamato: N-no... But those are
military officers and officials
from the Central Council...
What's going on?
There are dozens of times\nmore people than our elite\nsquad! At this rate...!
Yes, we're going to settle this\nall at once!
It stopped...?
I've accessed Darmizer'56's\ncontrol mechanism! It won't go\nberserk anymore!
Yamato: We did it... Did we\nactually pull it off...?
Yamato: It's our victory!!!!
Thank goodness, for a moment\nI thought we were lost...

Thanks to everyone's
cooperation, it looks like no
one was injured seriously.
Thank you all!
Elder's Granddaughter: No, to\nreceive such words from a\nGoddess... We are honored.

Young Man of the Nation: We
only fought because of you,
Goddess!! Seeing your bravery
boosts our morale! You truly
are a War Goddess!
I'm sorry for deceiving you all\nuntil now. We aren't gods or\nanything like that...
We are humans, just like you.
Young Man of the Nation:\nHuh...?

Our ancestors were born far
from here, overcoming many
disasters similar to the ones
you face now.

So, we are just ordinary
humans who happen to know a
few more survival skills and
bits of wisdom than you do.

Actually, I lived deep
underground. The surface
became a tainted land, no
longer fit for human life...
Yamato: ...I-Is that even\npossible?
Unfortunately...

But that is the result of my
father, my mother, and many
others thinking desperately to
pass hope on to the future.

There is despair that makes
you want to cling to the gods...
but only after you've done your
absolute best.
Even the gods won't smile upon\nthose who do nothing.

Iyo: The cause of the faith that
leads people to cling to our
nation's gods lies with us, the
Miko clan.
Elder: Lady Miko! You have\ncome here!? What is the\nmeaning of this...!

Iyo: To the travelers from
distant lands and everyone
here: thank you from the
bottom of my heart for saving
our nation from this crisis.
Iyo: And now... please, listen.
...!! Iyo, surely you aren't going\nto speak of the prophecy\nhere!?
Yamato: Lady Iyo! Please, don't\ndo this!!
Iyo: Yamato, stand back. I shall\ntell you everything... regarding\nthe sins of our Miko.

Elder: ...B-but, Lady Miko. Then
what were those prophecies...?
You were always guiding us on
the righteous path...!!

Iyo: By reading the prophecies
left by the First Miko, one can
predict the future to a certain
extent.

Iyo: Since they lack detail,
some Miko guided people by
passing them off as
prophecies. I am no exception.
Elder: ...What is this? Are you\nsaying you Miko have been\ndeceiving us all this time!
Isn't that a bit different?

I entered the Miko's shrine and
found piles of documents on
the country's situation, crop
yields, neighboring nations, and
new technologies...

I believe successive Miko used
those documents to find the
best path, guiding the nation
by calling it prophecy.
Unable to tell anyone, they\ncarried that heavy burden all\nalone...

Elder's Granddaughter: We
were just trying to take it easy
by leaving everything to the
Miko...

Young Man of the Nation:
Sorry... we didn't know. We
thought we just had to believe
in the Miko...
It is not entirely your fault.
Elder: Hmm?

The successive Priestesses
have underestimated the
strength of the people. They
were so desperate to handle
everything themselves that
they refused to rely on anyone.
Ichiyo, you were the same,
weren't you?
Ichiyo: ...!

Have you seen the people of
this country fight with
Dauntless Courage? They are
more reliable than you think.

Ichiyo: ...You are right. It seems
it was my own mindset, rather
than the country, that needed
to change.

Young Man: Then please, count
on us, Priestess! If we work
together, we can overcome
even poor harvests and
plagues!

Ichiyo: ...But, our clan of
Priestesses has continued to
deceive everyone for
decades...!

Elder's Granddaughter: ...Those
lies to protect us must have
been painful. From now on, we
won't just rely on you,
Priestess, but walk beside you.
Ichiyo, there isn't a single\nperson here who wants to\ncondemn you.

Besides, you've been reading
that mountain of literature.
Isn't your knowledge necessary
for this country's future?

Elder: ...I haven't lived this long
for nothing. I know a bit about
farming. I'll go call the other
elders.
Ichiyo: Elder...! Thank you so\nmuch.

I suppose this very moment
marks a new beginning for this
country. It's a view truly worthy
of the occasion!

This story has concluded. We
plan to release various other
stories in the future. Please
look forward to them.

Yamato: Food and plague
issues won't be solved
instantly, but meetings are
underway. It is all thanks to
everyone.

No, it was the hard work of the
elite troops that moved
people's hearts. We didn't do
anything...
You looked quite the part\nleading those elite troops,\nYamato.
Yamato: In that case, I am\neven more grateful to you\nboth.

Yamato: Without Reimi's words
back then, I'd still be struggling
and wouldn't have been able to
lead the troops like that...
The day before the final battle

Yamato, this elite unit you've
assembled is impressive.
They're well-disciplined and
have high morale. Are they
your subordinates?
Yamato: No, they are comrades\nfrom when I was stationed on\nthe northern border guard.

I heard from Ichiyo that this
country is under invasion, so
everyone is quite accustomed
to combat, aren't they?

Yamato: Yes. And everyone is
staking everything on the hope
that this battle will change this
country.
Staking everything?

Yamato: The border region was
already poor with little aid, but
this recent crop failure has
driven them into the worst
possible situation.

Yamato: If this war changes
the nation, we might save our
families from disease and
hunger. That is why morale is
so high.
Yamato, what about you?
Yamato: Me...?

...The idea that there is a
country willing to shelter Ichiyo
if a rebellion breaks out... that's
a lie, isn't it?
Yamato: ...!!

She intends to end this
rebellion through her own
execution, in order to create a
new nation.

Yamato: ...I am deeply sorry.
The Priestess forbade me from
discussing this, knowing it
would concern everyone.

Yamato, are you truly okay
with this? A reform built upon
the sacrifice of someone who
cares for this country so much!
Yamato: ............ It is not a\nmatter of whether I can accept\nit or not...

Yamato: The Priestess has
made her decision. As a
Guardian, I will fulfill my duty
with everything I have.
I can tell just by watching you\ndraw your bow. That your\nheart is filled with hesitation...

Even if it's just an act, you're
leading these soldiers. If a
commander is in that state,
won't everyone suffer?
If there are circumstances\nweighing on you, could you\nplease tell us?

Yamato: ...You truly are
straightforward people. It
seems I won't be able to
deceive you.

Yamato: ...The truth is, there
was one time when I attempted
to kidnap the Priestess and
flee.
That was about ten years ago,\nwhen the Priestess was still in\nher teens.

The country was in chaos, with
crop failures continuing in
various regions, just as they
are now.
She must have been thinking\nof any possible solution without\na moment's rest.

Seeing how terrible she looked,
I was determined to make her
drink the medicinal broth no
matter what.
So, I broke the taboo and\nstepped into the Priestess's\nshrine.
And there, I learned the truth\nof the Priestess and what lay\nwithin the shrine...

I urged everyone to tell the
public this burden was too
much for a teenage girl, but
she never once agreed.
And then, the incident\noccurred.

Driven to desperation by the
worsening food shortage,
frontier youths stormed the
Central Council.
Fires were breaking out all\nover this town.
As I protected her amidst the\nfleeing crowds, I realized this\nwas our chance.
Taking advantage of the chaos,\nI stole a horse and led her\naway.

Let's abandon this country
that places such a heavy
burden on you, and just live
the two of us together.
And as we rode, we talked\nabout what we wanted to do\nonce we crossed the border...
Yamato: While I was letting the\nhorse rest, she was gone.
So Ichiyo had already made up\nher mind about how she\nwanted to live at that age.
Yamato: From that moment on,\nI decided to live according to\nher resolve.
Yamato: I am the blade that\ncarries out her wishes. Even if\nshe desires death, I will fulfill it.
Is that how you're going to end\nup entrusting everything to\nIchiyo-san too?

If you give up on changing
Ichiyo-san's mind and stop
thinking, aren't you just like
everyone else in the country?
Yamato: ...!!
...Yamato-san. Won't you tell me\nwhat you're thinking?
Yamato: ...I...
Yamato: ...I want to protect\nLady Ichiyo...!! But if I do that,\nthe country she loves will...!
Then it's decided. We'll protect\nthem both. Lady Ichiyo and this\ncountry!

Even if it's reckless, if your
resolve is unwavering,
Yamato-san, a path will open.
I'll help you too!

Yamato: To think I've become
someone forcing such a heavy
burden upon the Priestess... I
am truly ashamed.

There must be a way to
protect this country and Lady
Ichiyo. As long as we keep
searching for that path
together...
Yamato: Yes. I will keep that in\nmy heart and continue to\ndevote myself to my duties.
Protect everything, huh...?\nReimi, you're starting to sound\na lot like Edge.
Eh!?
I guess it's true that married\ncouples start to resemble each\nother~. Onii-san is so happy!
Hmph, married... What are you\ntalking about, Crowe-san!! It's\nnot like that!!

Yamato: So Reimi, you have
someone precious to you as
well. I would very much like to
meet them.
Wait, Crowe! I told you,\nseriously, stop it!!

The prophecy to "hold a feast
to entertain the gods" was also
intended to centralize the
crops, wasn't it?

Ichiyo: Yes. That way, we can
buy crops from surplus areas
and sell them at low prices to
regions suffering from poor
harvests.
So, the Oracles are also skilled\nin economics.
Ichiyo: It is thanks to the\ndocuments left behind by the\nsuccessive Oracles.

It's not all resolved, but it
seems we aren't needed here
anymore. Shall we return to our
own journey?
What's wrong?

Something is still bothering me.
I want to know what on earth
was actually driving that
Korodaruma.
Maybe Coro's poor\nmaintenance?

That's not impossible, but they
say a special barrier was in
